title: Deactivate responsiveness of st.columns
body:
Hi, I'm using `st.columns` on `st.form`.

In mine desktop the widgets align. But in the mobile version not. 

I did some tests here and discovered that in the mobile version the app don't create the columns. 
Here are the [app link](https://guihungaro-streamlit-bug-streamlit-bug-columns-sk3jnd.streamlitapp.com/) and the [app repo](https://github.com/GuiHungaro/streamlit_bug)

**Desktop version:**

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/97532025/180021115-d0a0201e-eefb-4ab9-9328-ef2bf8700579.png)


**Mobile version:**
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/97532025/180021280-7d906165-844a-406b-a47c-54a51ee790e1.png)



**The code:**

```
import streamlit as st
with st.form("Test"):
    col1, col2, col3 = st.columns(3)
    with col1:
        st.write("col1")
        st.form_submit_button("Button 1")
    with col2:
        st.write("col2")
        st.form_submit_button("Button 2")
    with col3:
        st.write("col3")
        st.form_submit_button("Button 3")
```
 

Accept sugestions to solve this bug, maybe using css or markdown.

comments.body: [USER] Thanks for reporting this! `st.columns` are built to be responsive, meaning that it will switch to rendering the columns underneath each other at a certain display size. So, this is more of an enhancement request to add some capabilities to deactivate the responsiveness of columns.
facing same issue here. Is there a workaround to align elements horizontally on mobile?

Same problem here.
Wish there was a workaround for this.
Anyone figured out a clever workaround for this yet?

Please is there a workaround this issue?
Even if it demands using custom CSS!
Guys this behavior is really annoying. Absolutely thin columns with minimum information that obviously should fit mobile screen go vertical instead. Please fix
Is there a plan to fix this still? I've run into a lot of issues with column resizing.

> > As workaround, you can use CSS style:
> > ```python
> > st.write('''<style>
> > 
> > [data-testid="column"] {
> >     width: calc(33.3333% - 1rem) !important;
> >     flex: 1 1 calc(33.3333% - 1rem) !important;
> >     min-width: calc(33% - 1rem) !important;
> > }
> > </style>''', unsafe_allow_html=True)
> > ```
> 
> Thanks! This code works. But it still remains a problem for me. What if I need to arrange two columns with different widths in a row, for example:
> 
> ```python
> col1, col2 = st.columns([2, 1])
> ```

Alright, I finally found a strange way to solve this problem ~ XD
[USER] can you share with us the way please ? :)

Still an issue for me.

The work around are unusable if you have more than 1 set of columns.
very sad this is not implemented. I created an app with a goal to use it on mobile phone, and now it is unsuable. The whole design is gone and only 1 column rendered per row.

I think we can roll this into the slightly more general idea of configuring the threshold (#6592) to aggregate interest. The underlying problem is that the threshold is set by the overall width of the app and not the resultant width of the columns. e.g. It will flex the same with two columns or ten columns. So a responsiveness parameter that lets you either set an app-width threshold or column-width threshold would be nice (and could effectively allow disabling responsiveness by setting it sufficiently small).
This doesn't seem to work anymore - anyone else having issues?

I faced a similad need multiple times in my development experience with streamlit actually. Do you [USER] think that can we create a feature request for this? So this would be officially supported by Streamlit.

# Update We didn't implement a way to control the wrapping of `st.columns` yet but note that you can solve the original problem here more elegantly with the new layout parameters we added to `st.container` ([docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/layout/st.container)): ```python with st.container(horizontal=True): st.button("Button 1") st.button("Button 2") st.button("Button 3") ``` This will lay out the buttons side by side (without the big gap added by `st.columns`) and ensure they wrap only if there's not enough space:
ok so any input widget can be wrapped in st.container(horizontal=True) for mobiles scrrens?
important for mobile viewing

## Update

Streamlit 1.63+ will provide `wrap` parameter for `st.columns` to disable responsiveness:

```pyhon
col1, col2 = st.columns(2, wrap=False)
```
